neighbours.label: A word that sets up input in an exchange (questions, feedback, comments, contributions) as what comes next: ' asking', ' ask', ' contributes', 'gave great', in advice or praise about taking part; the same frames leading elsewhere stay lower.
fire: Good students learn by asking thoughtful questions in class.
Please leave us your honest feedback below.
Diners gave excellent feedback on the new menu.
Feel free to ask anything after the talk.
We urge readers to write a comment below.
You can help by contributing to the discussion.
Engage the speaker and ask for more details.
Members are invited to submit their comments to the board.
quiet: Bright students learn by reading the whole chapter at home.
Please leave your muddy boots by the door.
Diners left excellent tips on the new tables.
You may park anywhere after the talk.
He sat writing a letter to his mother.
Kind neighbours helped by carrying the boxes to the van.
A clerk kept asking the fare at every stop.
Members are required to pay their dues to the board.

short: word setting up questions, feedback, comments
notes: Probes: 0.47-0.96; 'asking the price' 0.09, 'writing a novel' 0.13, 'drank great wine' 0.12. The output direction suppresses ' questions', ' feedback', ' comments', ' requests' on the other pole, so this pole promotes them. One probe near miss ('Be a good driver') read 0.28 on ' a', so advice frames leak.
